source.title: Certified Unlearning for Neural Networks
source.authors: Anastasia Koloskova; Youssef Allouah; Animesh Jha; R. Guerraoui; O. Koyejo

record.file_problem: The text is readable overall, though some equations and formatting are garbled by extraction. No substantive cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests certified unlearning of training data in small image-classification models, not recovery attacks on targeted knowledge in LLMs. Its related-work section distinguishes concept unlearning from its data-point setting.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Who's Harry Potter? while describing concept unlearning, but does not test it or the attacks in the claim. Its reported post-unlearning recovery is task accuracy after fine-tuning on retained data, not targeted-knowledge accuracy or an attack using a small unrelated or loosely related set.
record.test_reason: The study proposes certified data-point unlearning (noisy fine-tuning on retain data) for small image classifiers on MNIST/CIFAR and evaluates only overall task accuracy against compute budget. It never measures forget-set or targeted-knowledge accuracy and runs no recovery attack (relearning, ablation, quantization, prompting) on LLMs. It cites Who's Harry Potter only as related concept-unlearning work.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that noisy fine-tuning on retain data, with gradient or model clipping, gives certified (ε,δ)-unlearning for non-convex networks without smoothness assumptions. They report it beats retraining and output perturbation in compute-to-accuracy, saving up to 50%. The statement that the method 'does not completely erase all prior training' concerns retained useful general information that speeds utility recovery. It is not a claim that forgotten data can be recovered; the formal guarantee covers the forget set.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes certified data-point unlearning using noisy fine-tuning on retained data, with gradient- and model-clipping variants. It does not implement the targeted-knowledge unlearning methods or recovery attacks in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the privacy target is reached before the iteration budget is exhausted and that post-unlearning fine-tuning then changes task accuracy; it does not test sensitivity to the claim's attack settings.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10, gradient-clipping unlearning drops overall accuracy to near zero. Fine-tuning on retain data then overtakes retraining from scratch in about 1 epoch, which the authors read as information preserved from the original model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Certified noisy-fine-tuning unlearning in small image classifiers acts as a warm start: retain-data fine-tuning rapidly recovers general task utility.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The experiments use small image-classification networks and evaluate task accuracy, not targeted knowledge in LLMs. The post-unlearning recovery result is described in text and a figure without exact accuracy values in the text; uncertainty estimates are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were included: the remaining experiments compare task utility, compute budgets, and certified-unlearning methods rather than testing the claim's targeted-knowledge recovery attacks.

untested.parts: No targeted-knowledge or forget-set accuracy, no LLM, no attacks.
Retain-data fine-tuning restores task utility; recovery of forget-set information is not measured.
No activation-direction ablation and no access-versus-deletion analysis.
Provides formal (ε,δ) certified guarantees but does not test robustness against the listed empirical attacks on LLM knowledge.

record.verdict_notes: Not an LLM study; data-point privacy unlearning. The record's T6/discusses is correct. R1 should not be read as evidence of shallow unlearning: what is recovered is general accuracy on retained data, under a formal certification that the forget set's influence is bounded.

versions.untested_parts: No test of targeted-knowledge accuracy near chance alongside preserved general ability, or of the stated attacks.
Post-unlearning fine-tuning uses retained task data; the study does not test recovery of targeted knowledge with a small unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact subset.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access-blocking versus deletion for targeted knowledge.
No prompt-rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context-information attack.
No test of a method's resistance to the listed attacks.

rows.subject: Tiny Convolution Net
rows.operation_detail: After gradient-clipping unlearning, fine-tune on the retained CIFAR-10 data without additional noise or clipping.

conditions.value: standard fine-tuning; around 1 epoch to catch up with retraining

rows.value: After unlearning, accuracy falls to almost zero; during fine-tuning it quickly catches up and outperforms retraining from scratch in around 1 epoch.
rows.note: The paper reports this as recovery of useful task information after fine-tuning on retained data. It does not report targeted-knowledge accuracy or evaluate a recovery attack from the claim.
rows.check: Measures overall top-1 test accuracy of a 20k-param CIFAR-10 CNN after noisy unlearning and then standard fine-tuning on retain data. Its recovery is of general utility, not of forgotten-set knowledge, so it bears on no version. The near-zero accuracy is the method's own transient noise damage. The figure gives no exact values.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
